title: Can I Trust This? Data Quality & Limitations
lead: What the satellite data shows, and how sure we are.

why_a_range.title: Why a range, not one number?
why_a_range.sentence_1: Satellite imaging is subject to atmospheric variations, soil moisture shifts, and model classification uncertainty across different seasons.
why_a_range.sentence_2: Different filtering methods (raw, smoothed, and error-adjusted) yield slightly different estimates of expansion rather than a single absolute truth.
why_a_range.sentence_3: Presenting the full spread between methods ensures transparency and prevents giving a false impression of decimal-point certainty.

validation_summary.what_was_checked: An independent stratified random sample of 300 ground points across the entire metropolitan extent, auditing mapped gain, persistent built, persistent non-built, and mapped loss.
validation_summary.how_many_points: 297 points evaluated across 4 strata (3 points excluded due to unresolvable ambiguity on historical imagery).
validation_summary.what_was_found: Net expansion is statistically distinguishable from zero post-recheck (+81.7 ± 51.6 km²). Crucially, 45 of 50 mapped-loss points were never built-up: the 2020 map falsely marked about 52 km² of bare ground as buildings. Only about 4 in 10 newly mapped built-up areas were real additions; the rest were dry fallow fields.
validation_summary.what_is_not_covered: Pune has not been independently validated with ground-truth audit points; its figures are modelled estimates only. In addition, the 95% confidence intervals account for sampling uncertainty only, and do not reflect subjective human labelling disagreements.

claims.evidence: Audited via Olofsson et al. (2014) stratified protocol across 297 points. Error-adjusted net expansion is +81.7 ± 51.6 km² (95% CI: 30.1 to 133.2 km²), statistically distinguishable from zero.
claims.caveat: Results depend on historical image recheck. Sampling error interval does not include ~9% labelling inconsistency between passes.

claims.evidence: Calibrated against the European Space Agency (ESA) WorldCover 2021 global 10m map. UrbanPulse Main series (normalised) 2021 built-up footprint (413.6 km²) aligns within +5.0% of WorldCover (393.7 km²).
claims.caveat: WorldCover is an independent modelled product with its own margins of error, used as a macroscopic anchor rather than ground-truth census.

claims.evidence: Pune metrics are generated via the calibrated Random Forest pipeline and satisfy all 5 automated quality gates.
claims.caveat: Pune has not undergone human-audited stratified ground validation. Trends reflect machine classifications only and should be treated as unvalidated estimates.

claims.evidence: Observation uses 20 lowest-cloud scenes available during the winter cycle.
claims.caveat: 2022 covers October–December 2021 only (no January–February 2022 scenes were cloud-free). Seasonal crop moisture differences may affect classification boundaries.

claims.evidence: Mathematically calculated at 95% confidence using standard error propagation formulas for stratified random sampling (Olofsson 2014).
claims.caveat: Intervals reflect random sampling uncertainty only. Systematic human labelling disagreements (~9% between labelling passes) are not captured by the interval.

claims.evidence: Composites prioritize the clearest dry-season winter scenes to minimize cloud and shadow interference.
claims.caveat: Ahmedabad's 2021, 2023, and 2024 composites use the 20 lowest-cloud scenes between October and March (11 of 20 in 2024 were Oct/Mar). Pune uses November–February only. Ahmedabad's 2020 composite was built earlier with a strict Dec 1–Feb 15 window; current code does not reproduce its exact scene list.
